 The Clerk of Courts Race in Palm Beach
 By Shaye Rosen 
 October 23, 2026 
 Facebook WhatsApp Linkedin X Email Copy URL 
 As Palm Beach County voters prepare for the November 3 election, the race for Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller has become one of the county’s most closely watched local contests. The election features Democratic candidate Yvette Drucker, a Boca Raton City Council member, and Republican Mike Caruso, the former Florida state representative who was appointed clerk in 2025. The race has drawn additional attention following Caruso’s suspension from office and arrest on felony charges in August 2026. Caruso has denied the allegations, and the charges have not established guilt. Despite the controversy, his name is expected to remain on the November ballot.
 What Does the Clerk of Courts Do?
 Although the position may receive less attention than races for governor or Congress, the Palm Beach County Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller plays an important role in residents’ daily lives.
 The office maintains court records, handles court-related payments and documents, records property transactions, issues marriage licenses and oversees important county financial responsibilities. As comptroller, the clerk also helps monitor county spending, maintain financial records and provide accountability for taxpayer dollars.
 These responsibilities affect residents across Palm Beach County, including Boca Raton. Property owners rely on accurate public records, people involved in court proceedings depend on the court system’s administrative services, and taxpayers have an interest in how county finances are managed.
 The clerk’s role therefore combines two major responsibilities: supporting the judicial system and helping ensure that public money is handled responsibly.
 Who Is Running?
 Yvette Drucker, Democrat
 Yvette Drucker is a Boca Raton City Council member and former deputy mayor who is running for the countywide clerk position. Her experience in municipal government gives her a background in local public service and the administrative responsibilities of government.
 Drucker initially pursued a state Senate campaign before switching to the clerk’s race in 2025. Her candidacy places a familiar local elected official in a countywide contest, expanding the race beyond Boca Raton’s municipal government.
 Voters evaluating Drucker can examine her record on the City Council, her experience with local government operations and her stated plans for managing court services, public records and county finances. Her campaign’s specific proposals should be reviewed directly to understand what changes she would prioritize if elected.
 Mike Caruso, Republican
 Mike Caruso became Palm Beach County Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller in August 2025 after Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed him to fill the vacancy left by Joe Abruzzo, who became county administrator. Before his appointment, Caruso served in the Florida House of Representatives and worked as a certified public accountant.
 During his tenure, Caruso highlighted efforts to improve fraud prevention, modernize financial processes, strengthen information technology security and improve public access to services. The clerk’s office also promoted its Property Fraud Alert program, which notifies participating property owners about potentially fraudulent activity involving their property records.
 However, Caruso’s tenure was interrupted in August 2026, when he was arrested on five felony charges and suspended from performing his official duties by DeSantis. Caruso has denied the allegations and remains presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.
 Shannon Ramsey-Chessman, who previously served as chief deputy clerk, was appointed to serve as clerk ad interim following his suspension.
 Why Is the Race Unusual?
 The circumstances surrounding Caruso’s suspension have created an unusual election situation. Although he no longer performs the duties of the office, his suspension did not automatically remove him as a candidate.
 According to reporting by Florida Politics, the deadline to replace his name on the November ballot passed after the Republican primary results were finalized. If Caruso withdraws, the Republican Party may designate a replacement under applicable election procedures, but Caruso’s printed name would remain on the ballot and votes cast for him would be credited to the party’s designated replacement.
 The situation has also drawn public and political attention to the distinction between being suspended from public office and being removed as a candidate. These are separate legal processes, meaning voters may encounter a candidate on the ballot who is not currently carrying out the responsibilities of the position.
 The developments have made the race about more than the candidates’ backgrounds and proposed administrative priorities. They have also raised questions about public accountability, the continuity of government services and how election rules operate under unusual circumstances.
 What Should Voters Consider?
 For voters in Boca Raton and throughout Palm Beach County, several issues are especially relevant when evaluating the candidates.
 Financial accountability: The clerk serves as the county comptroller, making financial oversight, accurate reporting and responsible management of taxpayer funds central responsibilities.
 Public records and fraud prevention: Property fraud and scams involving court-related services can affect residents directly. Voters can examine each candidate’s plans for protecting public records and helping residents identify fraudulent activity.
 Court access and customer service: The office handles services used by residents, attorneys, property owners and people involved in legal proceedings. Efficient processing, accessible information and clear communication are important measures of its performance.
 Technology and modernization: Maintaining secure digital records and improving online services can make government more accessible, but technological changes must also protect sensitive information.
 Experience and accountability: Voters can compare Drucker’s experience in municipal government with Caruso’s background in state government, accounting and his time in the clerk’s office. They can also review each candidate’s documented record, specific proposals and approach to public accountability.
 When Is Election Day?
 The general election is scheduled for Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller contest is countywide, so eligible Palm Beach County voters, including those living in Boca Raton, can participate.
 Voters should consult the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections for official ballot information, polling locations, early voting details and updates on election procedures.
 The clerk’s race demonstrates why local elections deserve attention even when they receive less coverage than national contests. The office manages court records, property information and public finances that affect residents throughout the county. Understanding the candidates, the responsibilities of the position and the circumstances surrounding the election can help voters make an informed decision on Election Day.
